title: Skill library audit and proposal

description.need: A library of written procedures drifts away from the code it describes and accumulates entries nobody has used in months, and neither drift nor disuse announces itself. The entry that has gone wrong is the dangerous one, because somebody will follow it and find out at the worst moment, while the missing entry only costs time. The obvious remedy makes it worse: retiring whatever nothing has called removes the entry that covers the rare situation first, since being rarely needed is what a rare situation looks like from a usage count.
description.input: What has changed in the codebase since the last audit, the entries as currently written, when each was last confirmed to still work as distinct from when it was last edited, and how often each is actually reached for.
description.core_action: Turn genuine drift or genuine disuse into a proposal a person can approve or reject, treating a low usage count as a question to ask rather than a verdict to act on, and capping each pass tightly enough that the review queue stays readable.
description.output: A small number of edit or deprecation proposals, each carrying the change in full, an entry marked deprecated with its replacement named rather than deleted where retirement is agreed, and nothing proposed that was declined recently.

activities.label: Enumerate every entry, not only the ones that changed
Read what changed in the code the entries describe
Count how often each entry is actually reached for
Decide which drift or disuse is worth proposing, within the cap
Offer each as an edit or a deprecation with the change in full

outcomes.statement: An entry that no longer matches the world it describes is corrected before somebody follows it.
success_criteria: Each entry carries when it was last confirmed to work, kept separate from when it was last edited, because an edit date says an entry is recent and says nothing about whether it is right.
An entry describing code that has moved is proposed as a concrete edit with the change in full, not flagged for somebody else to go and investigate.
An entry that is wrong is treated as more urgent than a gap where an entry is missing, because the wrong one will be followed and the missing one will not.

outcomes.statement: Disuse opens a question about an entry and never closes one, so the library gets smaller without losing the thing that covers the rare case.
success_criteria: A low usage count produces an enquiry naming what the entry covers and asking whether it is still wanted, never an automatic retirement.
Retirement happens in two steps: the entry is marked deprecated with its replacement named, and only later removed, with removal decided by what is still reaching for it rather than by a date.
What an entry is depended on for is not assumed to be what it declares, since another entry may rely on the shape of its output or on a name it uses, and neither is written down anywhere.

outcomes.statement: The person reading the proposals keeps reading them, pass after pass.
success_criteria: No pass exceeds the cap, and a pass that could have exceeded it says how many it held back rather than silently truncating.
A proposal the person has already declined is not offered again within the cooldown, and the reason it was declined is carried with the entry.
A pass that found no genuine drift and no genuine disuse says so, and the first pass over a library says it is establishing the inventory rather than reporting decay.

guidance: An entry that has gone wrong is worse than one that is missing, because somebody follows it. Keep two dates: when it was last edited, and when it was last confirmed to work, because the first says an entry is recent and says nothing about whether it is right. Treat low usage as a question, never a verdict; the entry nobody reaches for is often the one that covers the rare situation. Retire in two steps, and let what is still reaching for it decide the second.
use_cases: A library that grew through a year of enthusiastic writing, where nobody can now say which entries are still true and the safest working assumption has become that none of them are.

A team that reached for a procedure during an incident and found it describing a system that had been replaced, so the outage ran longer than it needed to and the library lost its credibility in one night.
A maintainer who wants to shrink the library and has only usage counts to work from, which would retire the entry covering the once a year situation before anything else.
A library whose entries quietly rely on each other, where removing the one nothing calls breaks three that were being used every week, because the dependency was never written down anywhere.
An operator who worked through a batch of proposals once, declined most of them, and found the same batch waiting the following week, and has not opened the proposals since.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Act when the code has moved enough that the written procedures could have drifted, or when a measurement window has passed with an entry going unreached. A fixed weekly slot audits an unchanged library and proposes nothing, which trains its reader to stop opening the proposals, and that costs more than the audit was worth.

personalization_needs: Where the library lives and what shape an entry takes, because a proposal in the wrong shape cannot be applied and will be declined for a reason that has nothing to do with its content.

How this operation marks that an entry was used, since the disuse half of the audit rests entirely on it and many operations have no convention at all, in which case that half is unmeasured rather than zero.
How many proposals this person can absorb per pass, which is what the cap is for and is a property of the reader rather than of the library.
Which entries this operation considers load bearing regardless of how often they are reached for, because that list is the guard against the audit retiring exactly the wrong thing.

input_schema.name: scan_window_days
input_schema.description: How far back to look for changes in the code the entries describe. It should follow how fast this codebase actually moves rather than a calendar: a window shorter than the pace of change makes every pass look quiet.

input_schema.name: strength_window_days
input_schema.description: The window over which an entry's use is counted. It has to be longer than the natural period of the work the entry covers, or a quarterly procedure reads as unused every single time it is measured.

input_schema.name: weak_skill_threshold
input_schema.description: Use at or below this in the measurement window makes an entry a question rather than a retirement. Zero is the usual setting and the most dangerous one to act on directly, because an entry nobody reached for may simply be the one that covers the situation nobody has been in yet.

input_schema.name: max_proposals_per_run
input_schema.description: Hard cap on proposals surfaced per pass. The cap protects the reader rather than the run, so a pass that hits it should say how many it held back instead of quietly presenting the cap as the finding.
